sentences.cn_text: 有些考古遗址历来都很容易观察到，例如希腊雅典的帕特农神庙、埃及吉萨的金字塔群以及英格兰南部的巨石阵。
sentences.en_text: Some archaeological sites have always been easily observable — for example, the Parthenon in Athens, Greece; the pyramids of Giza in Egypt; and the megaliths of Stonehenge in southern England.

sentences.cn_text: 但这些遗址只是例外情况。
sentences.en_text: But these sites are exceptions to the norm.

sentences.cn_text: 大多数考古遗址是通过细致搜寻而定位的,而许多其他遗址则是偶然发现的。
sentences.en_text: Most archaeological sites have been located by means of careful searching, while many others have been discovered by accident.

sentences.cn_text: 坦桑尼亚的早期原始人类遗址奥杜威峡谷,是由一位蝴蝶采集者于1911年意外跌入其深谷时发现的。20世纪70年代墨西哥城地铁施工期间,成千上万件阿兹特克文物重见天日。
sentences.en_text: Olduvai Gorge, an early hominid site in Tanzania, was found by a butterfly hunter who literally fell into its deep valley in 1911.Thousands of Aztec artifacts came to light during the digging of the Mexico City subway in the 1970s.

sentences.cn_text: 在另一个案例中,美国考古学家雷内·米利翁和乔治·考吉尔花费数年时间系统地绘制了位于墨西哥谷地、靠近现今墨西哥城的整座特奥蒂瓦坎古城的地图。
sentences.en_text: In another case, American archaeologists René Million and George Cowgill spent years systematically mapping the entire city of Teotihuacan in the Valley of Mexico near what is now Mexico City.

sentences.cn_text: 在公元600年左右的鼎盛时期,这座城市是世界上最大的人类聚居地之一。
sentences.en_text: At its peak around AD 600, this city was one of the largest human settlements in the world.

sentences.cn_text: 研究人员不仅绘制了该城广袤而华美的祭祀区域,还绘制了数百处普通民众居住的简朴公寓建筑群。
sentences.en_text: The researchers mapped not only the city’s vast and ornate ceremonial areas, but also hundreds of simpler apartment complexes where common people lived.

sentences.cn_text: 当地表没有任何可见物时,考古学家如何知道要在哪里寻找他们的目标?
sentences.en_text: How do archaeologists know where to find what they are looking for when there is nothing visible on the surface of the ground?

sentences.cn_text: 通常,他们会对大面积地形进行勘测和取样(进行试探性发掘),以确定在哪里挖掘能够获取有用信息。
sentences.en_text: Typically, they survey and sample (make test excavations on) large areas of terrain to determine where excavation will yield useful information.

sentences.cn_text: 勘测和试探性取样对于理解包含考古遗址的更广阔地貌环境也变得越来越重要。
sentences.en_text: Surveys and test samples have also become important for understanding the larger landscapes that contain archaeological sites.

sentences.cn_text: 勘测范围可以是单个大型聚落,也可以是整片地域景观。
sentences.en_text: Surveys can cover a single large settlement or entire landscapes.

sentences.cn_text: 在一个案例中,众多研究人员在洪都拉斯古玛雅城市科潘周边开展工作,通过使用航空照片和徒步勘测,定位了数百个小型乡村聚落和单独的住宅遗迹。
sentences.en_text: In one case, many researchers working around the ancient Maya city of Copán, Honduras, have located hundreds of small rural villages and individual dwellings by using aerial photographs and by making surveys on foot.

sentences.cn_text: 由此绘制的聚落地图显示,在公元500年至850年科潘走向衰亡期间,该城周边乡村人口的分布和密度发生了显著变化。
sentences.en_text: The resulting settlement maps show how the distribution and density of the rural population around the city changed dramatically between AD 500 and 850, when Copán collapsed.

sentences.cn_text: 为了找到遗址,当今的考古学家在很大程度上依赖系统的勘测方法以及各种高科技工具和技术。
sentences.en_text: To find their sites, archaeologists today rely heavily on systematic survey methods and a variety of high-technology tools and techniques.

sentences.cn_text: 机载技术,如飞机或航天器搭载的各类雷达和摄影设备,使考古学家能够在不进行挖掘的情况下了解地下情况。
sentences.en_text: Airborne technologies, such as different types of radar and photographic equipment carried by airplanes or spacecraft, allow archaeologists to learn about what lies beneath the ground without digging.

sentences.cn_text: 航空勘测可定位一般性关注区域或较大型的埋藏遗迹,例如古代建筑或农田。
sentences.en_text: Aerial surveys locate general areas of interest or larger buried features, such as ancient buildings or fields.

sentences.cn_text: 然而,大多数考古遗址是由专门前往寻找它们的考古学家所发现的。
sentences.en_text: Most archaeological sites, however, are discovered by archaeologists who have set out to look for them.

sentences.cn_text: 这样的搜寻可能耗时数年。
sentences.en_text: Such searches can take years.

sentences.cn_text: 英国考古学家霍华德·卡特从其他遗址所获信息中得知埃及法老图坦卡蒙陵墓的存在。
sentences.en_text: British archaeologist Howard Carter knew that the tomb of the Egyptian pharaoh Tutankhamun existed from information found in other sites.

sentences.cn_text: 卡特在帝王谷的废墟中筛选了七年,最终于1922年找到了该陵墓。
sentences.en_text: Carter sifted through rubble in the Valley of the Kings for seven years before he located the tomb in 1922.

sentences.cn_text: 19世纪末,英国考古学家阿瑟·埃文斯爵士在希腊雅典的古董商店中反复搜寻。
sentences.en_text: In the late 1800s British archaeologist Sir Arthur Evans combed antique dealers’ stores in Athens, Greece.

sentences.cn_text: 他在寻找那些被认为属于古代迈锡尼文化的微型雕刻印章,该文化在公元前1400年至1200年间统治着希腊。
sentences.en_text: He was searching for tiny engraved seals attributed to the ancient Mycenaean culture that dominated Greece from the 1400s to 1200s BC.

sentences.cn_text: 埃文斯对这些雕刻的解读最终使他于1900年在克里特岛发现了克诺索斯的米诺斯王宫。
sentences.en_text: Evans’s interpretations of these engravings eventually led him to find the Minoan palace at Knossos (Knosós), on the island of Crete, in 1900.

sentences.cn_text: 地面勘测使考古学家能够精确定位挖掘成功率高的地点。
sentences.en_text: Ground surveys allow archaeologists to pinpoint the places where digs will be successful.

sentences.cn_text: 大多数地面勘测需要大量步行,寻找诸如陶器小碎片之类的地表线索。
sentences.en_text: Most ground surveys involve a lot of walking, looking for surface clues such as small fragments of pottery.

sentences.cn_text: 这些勘测通常还包括一定量的挖掘工作,以在地貌景观的选定点位检测埋藏物。
sentences.en_text: They often include a certain amount of digging to test for buried materials at selected points across a landscape.

sentences.cn_text: 考古学家还可以使用地面雷达、磁场记录仪和金属探测器等技术手段来定位埋藏的遗迹。
sentences.en_text: Archaeologists also may locate buried remains by using such technologies as ground radar, magnetic-field recording, and metal detectors.

sentences.cn_text: 考古学家通常使用计算机绘制遗址及其周边地貌景观的地图。
sentences.en_text: Archaeologists commonly use computers to map sites and the landscapes around sites.

sentences.cn_text: 二维和三维地图是规划发掘工作、呈现遗址面貌以及展示考古研究成果的有用工具。
sentences.en_text: Two- and three-dimensional maps are helpful tools in planning excavations, illustrating how sites look, and presenting the results of archaeological research.
